turns.customer: For snowshoeing in deep snow, Frostline winter boots or Ridgeline Mid hiking boots? How cold can each handle?
turns.reply: Go with the Frostline Winter Boot for deep-snow snowshoeing. It's an insulated snow boot rated to -30°C (temperature rating -30°C), waterproof, leather and rubber, 1600 g, 4.6 stars, $199.00, and in stock (sizes 7–12 in black). Note size 12 and 8 are low stock. The Ridgeline Mid Hiking Boot ($179.00, 1200 g, waterproof, 4.5 stars) has no insulation or cold rating, so it isn't suited to cold, snowy conditions. So there's no meaningful comparison — the Frostline is the right call for the cold.
